mechanism_narrative: Sustained decline in WORKPLACES mobility over four consecutive weeks signals persistent remote work adoption or economic contraction. This reduces commuter-adjacent retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -13.4% to -17.7% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases or remains flat over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining below -15%.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated PARKS mobility (>45% above baseline) indicates outdoor leisure substitution for indoor retail. When PARKS exceeds 45% for two consecutive weeks, consumers redirect discretionary spending away from retail venues, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above 45% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at 51.9% in t-0w, 50.4% in t-2w, 45.4% in t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next 14 days while PARKS remains above 45%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility decline accelerates week-on-week (from -16.3% to -20.0%), indicating reduced commuting and urban center access. This contraction in transit use directly constrains retail foot traffic in transit-adjacent retail zones over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -19% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined from -16.3% to -20.0% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -18%.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility (6.4-8.9% above baseline) combined with declining RETAIL_REC indicates consumers prioritize essential shopping over discretionary retail. When essential-goods mobility remains elevated while retail declines, essential-shopping behavior crowds out discretionary retail for the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 6% while RETAIL_REC is below -12%
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stable at 6.4-8.9%, RETAIL_REC stable at -12.1% to -13.9%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains between 6% and 9%.

mechanism_narrative: Winter onset in Melbourne (mid-July) drives outdoor leisure substitution (PARKS at 51.9%) and reduced transit use (-20.0%). This seasonal shift toward outdoor activity and away from enclosed retail venues will persist, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS elevated at 51.9%, TRANSIT at -20.0% in winter season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining above 45% and TRANSIT below -18%.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent RESIDENTIAL mobility near zero (0.0% in t-0w) combined with declining WORKPLACES (-17.7%) suggests policy-driven or health-driven constraints on mobility remain in place. These constraints will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next week as behavioral adaptation persists.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days while RESIDENTIAL remains within ±1% of baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of WORKPLACES decline (-17.7%) and TRANSIT decline (-20.0%) over the past four weeks indicates a structural shift in commuting patterns. If this dual decline continues, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed as the retail ecosystem loses commuter-driven traffic.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT decline by >1 percentage point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next 14 days if both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT decline further.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility spike to 51.9% in t-0w represents a threshold breach in outdoor-leisure substitution. Once PARKS exceeds 50%, consumer preference shifts decisively toward outdoor activities, and this behavioral reallocation will suppress RETAIL_REC recovery for the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 1 percentage point over the next 14 days while PARKS remains above 50%.
